speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has posed the gravest challenge for Singapore since independence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are confronting an unprecedented public health as well as economic crisis, with serious social consequences.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To get through the crisis and to emerge stronger and better, a concerted whole-of-society response needs to be led by the Government, with all Singaporeans playing their part.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This in turn requires a well-coordinated whole-of-Government effort, to navigate our way through the crisis, and to build back a better Singapore post-crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this challenging and uncertain environment, the Strategy Group organises the Public Service to develop and implement the Government's key policy priorities, in a coherent and coordinated manner.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond this, the Government also needs to adjust its policy responses to the new challenges and opportunities that have arisen from this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The pandemic has exacerbated geopolitical tensions, and altered the regional and global economic landscape.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A comprehensive review of the Government's medium-term policy agenda is needed, in order to tackle new challenges but also seize new opportunities, so that Singapore can manage this crisis well, and continue to thrive in a post-COVID-19 world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the midst of crisis, the Strategy Group will organise the cross-Ministry effort to review our policy agenda and set new ambitions for our future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will work with social agencies to review our social support policies in the light of the impact of COVID-19, especially to help vulnerable groups that have been more adversely affected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will form the basis of a refreshed social compact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Given that climate change is also a storm of great proportions, we will also review our infrastructure plans for a sustainable city, taking into consideration new industry needs and emerging new norms of working and living.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Tackling these complex challenges will require closer alignment across different policy areas, stronger sense-making capabilities, and effective implementation of the policy agenda.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will have tighter co-ordination between our economic and social policies, to ensure that Singaporeans can access jobs and opportunities in the post-COVID-19 economy, with vulnerable groups of workers receiving additional support, and social mobility continuing to be a feature of our society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To strengthen our sense-making capabilities, we are growing new capabilities in data analytics and citizen engagement to better understand the concerns of our citizens, so that we can develop better, more citizen-centric policies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore continues to face stark demographic realities, including low birth rates and an ageing population.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Local workforce growth will slow over the next decade.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 has intensified some of these challenges, for example with couples delaying their marriage and parenthood plans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government remains committed to keeping Singaporeans at the heart of our population strategies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also partner with employers and the community to cushion the impact of COVID-19 on the marriage and parenthood plans of young couples.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to take a calibrated approach to immigration and maintain a careful balance in our foreign worker flows.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We welcome those who can contribute to our society and want to make Singapore their home, while ensuring that our policies allow Singaporeans to benefit from better jobs and opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To build a cohesive society, we will strengthen efforts to integrate new members of our community and help them adapt to the Singaporean way of life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must manage the disruptions caused by climate change, which may be more protracted than the impact of COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue with efforts to enable Singapore's transition to a sustainable, low-carbon, and climate and resource resilient future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To do so, we will continue to actively support global climate action, as no one country can prevent climate change alone.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Notwithstanding the disruptions and uncertainties brought about by COVID-19, we remain committed to achieve these goals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To enable our low-carbon transition, we are among other initiatives, studying ways to deploy technologies such as Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS), exploring the use of hydrogen, and pushing the bounds of ambition in solar deployment within our urban environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The fundamental shifts to a post-COVID-19 "new normal" also present new opportunities to advance our sustainability agenda.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will study green recovery pathways to rebuild our economy, in line with our long-term low-emissions aspirations, so that we not only emerge stronger but also advance our sustainability agenda.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, this Government has maintained focus on serving Singaporeans well both today and in the long term.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our capability in long-term strategic planning and foresight has served us well, and will remain essential as we navigate this crisis and chart our path beyond.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have outlined the broad strategies we will adopt, including for population and climate action, and the relevant agencies have provided more details on specific plans under their charge.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More than ever, Government, individuals, communities, and businesses must each do our part and work together, to overcome the pandemic and build a better and stronger post-COVID-19 future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In responding to the immense challenges at hand, and shaping our plans for tomorrow, we look forward to Singaporeans partnering with the Government to realise our hopes and dreams for a better Singapore.
